202	
203	### Authoring rules
204	
205	1. **`inputs.model` MUST be present and MUST be copied from `Data.Node.inputDefaults.model`.** Copy the blob verbatim — do not abbreviate, do not omit fields, do not invent fields that aren't there. The current deployment-node blob is `{ id, modelName, modelDisplayName, folderKey, folderName, folderPath, description }`; source every field from the actual `registry get` response, not from memory (older docs showed `fullyQualifiedName` / `kind` / `type` / `detailsUrl` / `async*` fields — these are NOT present on deployment nodes; do not add them). The `schema-definition` form section binds `inputs.model` to the `ixp-model-taxonomy` custom component, which destructures `modelName` and `folderKey` out of it. If `inputs.model` is undefined, clicking the node in Studio Web crashes the property panel with `Cannot destructure property 'modelName' of 't' as it is undefined` — and `flow validate` fails on it too (`ixp-node`: `inputs.model must be an object with non-empty string modelName and folderKey`).
206	   - **`inputs.model.modelName` MUST be a non-empty string.** For many published/OOB deployments `inputDefaults.model.modelName` comes back `null`, with the name carried in `inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName` instead. When `modelName` is `null`/empty, set `inputs.model.modelName` to `modelDisplayName`. This is NOT synthesis — `modelDisplayName` is the model's own name from the same blob (and matches the flat `inputDefaults.modelName`). The `ixp-node` validator rejects a `null`/empty `inputs.model.modelName` (`flow validate` fails), and Studio Web crashes on it.
207	2. **Flat mirrors stay alongside `inputs.model`.** `modelName`, `projectName`, `folderKey`, `folderName` are surfaced as disabled text fields in the `ixp-model` form section and are read directly from `inputs.*`, not from `inputs.model.*`.
208	3. **`fileRef` is the only schema-required input** (`inputDefinition.required: ["fileRef"]`). Use `=js:$vars.<upstream>.output.<field>` per Critical Rule #13. The upstream `<field>` variable MUST be declared `type: "file"` — `type: "object"` breaks attachment binding and faults extraction even when the `fileRef` expression itself is correct. See [Wiring `fileRef`](#wiring-fileref--file-variable-bound-to-the-trigger).
209	4. **`outputs.output` AND `outputs.error` MUST both be present** — copy the fixed four-field literals from [Final shape](#final-shape); they are identical for every IxP node and need no `registry get` lookup. **`flow validate` hard-fails on the omission** — `ixp-node` emits `[nodes[<nodeId>].outputs.output] outputs.output must be present on the instance`, and the matching error for `outputs.error`.
210	5. **No top-level `model` on the instance.** Studio Web–authored .flow files never carry one; the BPMN-format `model` envelope (with `context`, `version`, `inputs`, `outputs`) is emitted at serialize time only.
211	6. **`inputs` MUST NOT contain `digitizationMode`, `documentTaxonomy`, `attachmentId`, `fileName`, or `mimeType`.** These five fields were on a prior schema and have been removed from the standalone IxP node. Including them is the most common training-data-recall mistake. The serializer defaults `digitizationMode` to `fileUpload` internally — there is no scenario where you should set it on the instance.
212	7. **Every edge carries all five keys** — `id`, `sourceNodeId`, `sourcePort`, `targetNodeId`, `targetPort`. The node-reference keys are `sourceNodeId` / `targetNodeId`, not `source` / `target`. Port names are under [Registry Validation](#registry-validation).
213	
214	The `definitions[]` entry is copied verbatim from `registry get` (`Data.Node`) — every key, including `sortOrder`, which the schema requires on each definition. Critical Rule #7 applies unchanged.
215	
216	> **`uip maestro flow validate` enforces the Authoring rules above** via the `ixp-node` validator. Failures surface as `severity: "error"` issues with `path` like `nodes[<nodeId>].inputs.model` and a self-contained `message` describing the violation — fix the `.flow` file, not the validator. A common failure is `inputs.model must be an object with non-empty string modelName and folderKey` — this fires when `inputDefaults.model.modelName` was `null` and copied through verbatim; fix it by setting `inputs.model.modelName` from `inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName` (Authoring rule #1), not by relaxing the validator. The registry's `inputDefinition.properties` is the schema of the property catalog, not a license to override the rules: `digitizationMode`, `documentTaxonomy`, `attachmentId`, `fileName`, and `mimeType` are NOT returned by `registry get` and must not be set on the instance.
217	
218	### `inputs.fileRef` vs the emitted `model.inputs[]` body
219	
220	`inputs.fileRef` is the source of truth. At BPMN serialize time, `packages/services/src/serialization/uipath-extension.ts:handleIxpExtraction` wraps the value into a `model.inputs[]` entry with target `bodyField` and body `{"downloadedFileOutput": <fileRef>}`. Edit `inputs.fileRef` only; never hand-edit the BPMN body.
221	
222	### Wiring `fileRef` — file variable bound to the trigger
223	
224	The canonical canvas-produced shape is a flow `in` variable of `type: "file"` bound to the trigger via `triggerNodeId`, with the IxP node's `fileRef` referencing it through the trigger's output:
225	
226	```json
227	"variables": {
228	  "globals": [
229	    {
230	      "id": "disputedInvoice",
231	      "direction": "in",
232	      "type": "file",
233	      "triggerNodeId": "start"
234	    }
235	  ]
236	}
237	```
238	
239	Then on the IxP node:
240	
241	```json
242	"inputs": {
243	  "fileRef": "=js:$vars.start.output.disputedInvoice",
244	  ...
245	}
246	```
247	
248	Populate that variable at runtime with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <variableId>=<localPath>` (example: `--attachment disputedInvoice=./path/to/invoice.pdf`). The CLI uploads the file and binds it as a `{ ID, FullName, MimeType, Metadata }` Attachment object — keys are case-sensitive; `ID` is uppercase, not `Id`. The flag is repeatable; the `<variableId>` (left of `=`) must match a `variables.globals[]` entry's `id` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](../../../../shared/cli-commands.md#pre-flight---attachment-binding). Do not declare the variable as `type: "object"`, do not reference it as `=js:$vars.<variableId>` directly without the trigger output path, and do not pass a bare GUID/URL/path/`.ID`/`.FullName`.
249	
250	### Optional `attachment` input (Orchestrator job attachments)
251	
252	`inputDefinition.properties.attachment` accepts `{ ID, FullName, MimeType, Metadata }` for flows that consume Orchestrator job attachments. There is no form UI for this path on the standalone node today — set it programmatically in `inputs.attachment` if needed. `ID` is the only required field. Validate end-to-end on your tenant before relying on this path. This input does NOT replace `fileRef` — extraction reads `fileRef` regardless, and `fileRef` must carry the attachment object itself, never `<attachment>.ID`.
253	
254	## Accessing Output
255	
256	The extraction result is stored at `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. The IxP node's BPMN serializer maps the extraction service's `result` field directly to this variable (`source: '=result'`), so **the `result` wrapper is stripped** — `output` IS the extraction-result object, with no further wrapping.
257	
258	Top-level keys of `$vars.{nodeId}.output`:
259	
260	- `ExtractionResult` — `{ DocumentId, ResultsVersion, ResultsDocument }`. `ResultsDocument.Fields[]` carries the trained model's extracted values; `ResultsDocument.Tables[]` carries tabular extractions.
261	- `ExtractorPayloads` — provider-specific raw payloads.
262	- `BusinessrulesResults[]` — business-rule evaluation results, when configured.
263	
264	Each `Fields[]` element is shaped:
265	
266	```json
267	{
268	  "FieldId": "string",
269	  "FieldName": "string",
270	  "FieldType": "string",
271	  "IsMissing": false,
272	  "Values": ["string"],
273	  "Confidence": 95
274	}
275	```
276	
277	Read field values via `find` against `FieldName`, then index into `Values[]`:
278	
279	```javascript
280	// In a Script node after the IxP node
281	const fields = $vars.extractInvoiceFields.output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields || [];
282	const total = fields.find(f => f.FieldName === 'invoiceTotal')?.Values?.[0];
283	const vendor = fields.find(f => f.FieldName === 'vendor')?.Values?.[0];
284	return { total, vendor };
285	```
286	
287	Sibling error variable: `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — populated when extraction fails *and* the `error` port is wired (`supportsErrorHandling: true`). Mapped from the service response's `Error` field (`source: '=Error'`).
288	
289	### Wrong shapes the agent tends to invent
290	
291	These all pass `flow validate` and fail silently at runtime:
292	
293	- **Wrong:** `output.result.ExtractionResult.…` — there is no `result` wrapper at runtime; `=result` strips it before the value is assigned to `output`.
294	- **Wrong:** `output.<fieldName>` flat — extracted fields are not top-level properties of `output`; they live under `output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields[]` and are keyed by `FieldName`.
295	- **Wrong:** `output.ExtractionResult.Fields` — `Fields[]` is two levels under `ExtractionResult` (`output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields`), not one.
296	
297	Studio Web's variable picker renders `output.ExtractionResult` as opaque and does NOT surface the nested `ResultsDocument.Fields[]` shape. The path above is the source of truth — copy it from this doc, not from picker autocomplete or `outputDefinition.output.schema` (the registry schema describes the pre-`=result` wrapper, not the runtime variable).
298	
299	### Trained-model field taxonomy
300	
301	The `FieldName` values present in `ResultsDocument.Fields[]` depend on the trained IxP model's taxonomy and are NOT exposed through `uip maestro flow registry get` (the registry's `outputDefinition.output.schema` describes the wrapper envelope shape, not the per-model trained fields). Get them from the deployment:
302	
303	```bash
304	uip ixp deployments get-taxonomy --folder-key <folderKey> "<modelName>" --output json
305	```
306	
307	Both args come from the `registry get` response you already fetched in [Build procedure](#build-procedure--copy-from-registry-get-do-not-construct-from-memory): `--folder-key` ← `Data.Node.inputDefaults.folderKey`; `<modelName>` (positional) ← `Data.Node.inputDefaults.modelName`. No additional discovery step. Requires `uip login`; the command uses the user Bearer to call the same DU-App route that Studio Web's "Schema definition" panel uses.
308	
309	Response shape:
310	
311	```json
312	{
313	  "documentTaxonomy": {
314	    "documentTypes": [
315	      {
316	        "fields": [
317	          {
318	            "fieldId": "string",
319	            "fieldName": "string",
320	            "type": "Text",
321	            "components": []
322	          }
323	        ]
324	      }
325	    ]
326	  }
327	}
328	```
329	
330	`type` is one of `Text`, `Date`, `Number`, `Set`, `FieldGroup`. `components[]` is populated only when `type` is `FieldGroup` and carries sub-fields with the same shape recursively.
331	
332	**camelCase → PascalCase translation.** The taxonomy response uses `fieldName` (camelCase); runtime `Fields[]` elements use `FieldName` (PascalCase). The string *contents* match — design-time `"Birth Date"` is `FieldName: "Birth Date"` at runtime — but the wrapper key changes case. Translate the key, not the value, when going from `get-taxonomy` output to runtime `Fields[].FieldName` lookups.
333	
334	Agent call sequence:
335	
336	1. `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp" --output json` — list IxP nodes.
337	2. `uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --output json` — read `Data.Node.inputDefaults.{folderKey, modelName}` (already done as part of [Build procedure](#build-procedure--copy-from-registry-get-do-not-construct-from-memory)).
338	3. `uip ixp deployments get-taxonomy --folder-key <folderKey> "<modelName>" --output json` — read `documentTaxonomy.documentTypes[].fields[].fieldName`.
339	4. Author downstream consumers with `$vars.<id>.output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields.find(f => f.FieldName === '<fieldName from step 3>')?.Values?.[0]`.
340	
341	If the command fails (login expired, deployment not yet published, transient failure), fall back to defensive `find`-by-`FieldName` patterns with assumed field names and surface the assumptions to the user under **Open Questions**. Do NOT substitute a one-off extraction or IxP-product-UI inspection in the agent loop — `get-taxonomy` is the agent-loop path.
342	
343	## Landing the node when you cannot fully configure it
344	
345	**The extraction step must ALWAYS land a node — never drop it because configuration is incomplete.** A greenfield/exploration turn, an unwired upstream, a "you don't need a working flow" instruction, or an unconfirmed model are NOT reasons to skip it. The common failure is landing the steps around extraction while the extraction node itself goes missing.
346	
347	- **Model published** (`registry search "uipath.ixp"` returns entries) → land the real `uipath.ixp.*` node. When you can't finish configuring it this turn, still build the instance from `registry get` (copy `inputs.model` and the fixed `outputs` literal — no user input needed), set `inputs.fileRef` to a placeholder expression, and defer the model choice, `fileRef` source, and taxonomy to **Open Questions**. Do NOT downgrade to `core.logic.mock` — a published model exists, so land the real node.
348	- **No model published** (`Data: []`) → land a `core.logic.mock` placeholder per [If the Model Does Not Exist Yet](#if-the-model-does-not-exist-yet).
349	
350	## If the Model Does Not Exist Yet
351	
352	Trigger: `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp"` returns `Data: []`, OR the only matches are `uipath.agent.resource.tool.ixp.*` (agent-tool variant — not a flow extraction node).
353	
354	Action: insert a `core.logic.mock` placeholder via Direct JSON edit and stop. Do not iterate on registry searches.
355	
356	1. Fetch the definition: `uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.mock --output json`. Copy `Data.Node` verbatim into `definitions[]` if not already present.
357	2. Add a node to `nodes[]` with a stable id (e.g. `extractContractFieldsMock`), `type: "core.logic.mock"`, and a `display.label` whose **leading phrase** describes the work in the user's domain (e.g. `Extract Contract Fields`) rather than the underlying technology (`IxP Extraction`, `Run IxP`). The parenthetical may name IxP — e.g. `Extract Contract Fields (mock — IxP model not yet published)`.
358	3. Add a `layout.nodes` entry at `position: { x: 400, y: 144 }`, size `96x96`.
359	4. Wire edges per the parent [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) guide. `core.logic.mock` is a no-op pass-through — no `inputs`, no `outputs` block, no `bindings_v2.json` changes.
360	5. **Wire downstream consumers against the mock with `$vars` references, not static values.** Scripts, decisions, and end-node mappings that follow the mock MUST reference `$vars.{mockNodeId}.output` (the mock's only port) instead of hard-coded returns. Example: a script that summarises the (future) extraction writes `return { vendor: $vars.extractInvoiceFieldsMock.output.vendorName };`, not `return { ok: "OK" };`. This keeps the **node-graph** swap-ready — node IDs, edge shapes, and the `output` port name stay intact when the mock is replaced. **Field-access paths inside downstream scripts WILL need rewriting at swap time** — the real IxP `output` is shaped as `{ ExtractionResult: { ResultsDocument: { Fields: [...] } } }` (see [Accessing Output](#accessing-output)), so flat-field accessors against the mock become structured `Fields.find(f => f.FieldName === '<name>')?.Values?.[0]` lookups against the real node. Surface the post-swap rewrite as a follow-up under **Open Questions**.
361	6. Run `uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json` once after all edits complete.
362	
363	Surface the missing model in the **Open Questions** section of the architectural plan: the user must train and publish the IxP extraction model via the IxP product before the flow can run. After publishing, follow the [mock replacement procedure](../../editing-operations-json.md#replace-a-mock-with-a-real-resource-node) to swap the mock for the real IxP node.
364	
365	## Classifier Variant
366	
367	IxP also exposes classifier models (type `Classifier`) that label documents rather than extracting named fields. Classifier models share the `uipath.ixp.*` node-type pattern but produce a different `output` shape (classification labels, not field values). **Classifier configuration is not covered in this file** — if the user needs classification, flag it as a prerequisite and defer to a future revision of this impl.md.
368	
369	## Debug
370	
371	| Error | Cause | Fix |
372	| --- | --- | --- |
373	| Node type not found in registry | Model not published, or registry cache stale | Run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
374	| `model.context` rejected by runtime | `folderKey` or `modelName` missing from `inputs` (the context array is built from these) | Confirm `inputs.modelName` and `inputs.folderKey` are populated. |
375	| Empty `$vars.{nodeId}.output` | Model's taxonomy doesn't match the document, or extraction silently returned no fields | Inspect the raw API response via `$vars.{nodeId}.error` first; if no error, run the extraction against the same document on the IxP product UI to compare |
376	| `fileRef` not resolving | Expression references an upstream variable that isn't wired, or the upstream node didn't produce a file output | Verify the upstream node exports a file reference and that the `=js:$vars.{upstreamId}.output.<field>` expression matches |
377	| `[430002] Invalid input on document extraction operation` at debug | `fileRef` bound to the attachment's `.ID` (or another scalar) instead of the attachment object — `flow validate` does not catch this | Bind the whole object: `=js:$vars.<upstream>.output.<attachment>` — drop the `.ID` |
378	| `[430002] Invalid input on document extraction operation` at debug, backend detail `'downloadedFileOutput' is missing the required 'ID' field` | The `fileRef` expression is correct, but the source flow input is declared `"type": "object"` instead of `"type": "file"` — the attachment has nowhere to bind, so the variable holds a plain JSON object | Declare the input `type: "file"`. See [Wiring `fileRef`](#wiring-fileref--file-variable-bound-to-the-trigger). |
379	| Extraction failed | Underlying IxP model errored (unsupported MIME type, corrupted file, service-side failure) | Check `$vars.{nodeId}.error.detail` for the IxP service response |
380	| `uip maestro flow node configure` rejects with "not a connector type node" | Expected — IxP is not a connector. | Edit `inputs.*` in the `.flow` JSON directly. |
381	| Studio Web: "Cannot destructure property 'modelName' of 't' as it is undefined" when clicking the node | `inputs.model` blob is missing or undefined. The `schema-definition` form section binds `inputs.model` to the `ixp-model-taxonomy` component, which destructures `modelName` and `folderKey` out of it. When `inputs.model` is missing, the destructure throws. | Copy `definition.inputDefaults.model` verbatim into the node instance's `inputs.model`. The blob carries `id`, `modelName`, `modelDisplayName`, `folderKey`, `folderName`, `folderPath`, `description`. See [JSON Structure](#json-structure). |
382	| `flow validate` error `inputs.model must be an object with non-empty string modelName and folderKey` | `inputDefaults.model.modelName` was `null` (common for published/OOB deployments) and copied verbatim into `inputs.model`. | Set `inputs.model.modelName` from `inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName` (Authoring rule #1). `folderKey` is normally populated in the blob; if it too is empty, take it from the flat `inputDefaults.folderKey`. |
383

1	# Decision Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.decision`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.decision --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output ports `true` and `false`, required input `expression`. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	```json
18	{
19	  "id": "checkStatus",
20	  "type": "core.logic.decision",
21	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
22	  "display": { "label": "Check Status" },
23	  "inputs": {
24	    "expression": "$vars.fetchData.output.statusCode === 200"
25	  }
26	}
27	```
28	
29	## Adding / Editing
30	
31	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs`.
32	
33	## Expression Examples
34	
35	```javascript
36	// Simple comparison
37	$vars.fetchData.output.statusCode === 200
38	
39	// Boolean field
40	$vars.processData.output.isValid
41	
42	// Compound condition
43	$vars.httpCall.output.statusCode === 200 && $vars.httpCall.output.body.count > 0
44	
45	// String check
46	$vars.classify.output.category === "urgent"
47	
48	// Null check
49	$vars.lookupUser.output.user !== null
50	```
51	
52	## Wiring
53	
54	Output ports: `true` and `false`. Both branches must be wired. See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.
55	
56	## Debug
57	
58	| Error | Cause | Fix |
59	| --- | --- | --- |
60	| Expression does not evaluate to boolean | Expression returns non-boolean value | Ensure expression uses comparison operators (`===`, `>`, etc.) |
61	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
62	| Only one branch wired | Missing true or false edge | Add the missing edge — both branches are required |
63

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |
100

commands.result_summary: 1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 580 581 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 582 583 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 584 585 ```json 586 { 587 "id": "myScript.output", 588 "type": "object", 589 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 590 }, 591 { 592 "id": "myScript.error", 593 "type": "object", 594 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 595 } 596 ``` 597 598 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output variables: 617 618 ```json 619 { 620 "variables": { 621 "globals": [ 622 { 623 "id": "inputItems", 624 "direction": "in", 625 "type": "array", 626 "subType": "object", 627 "defaultValue": [], 628 "description": "Items to process" 629 }, 630 { 631 "id": "processedCount", 632 "direction": "inout", 633 "type": "number", 634 "defaultValue": 0 635 }, 636 { 637 "id": "result", 638 "direction": "out", 639 "type": "object", 640 "description": "Processing summary" 641 } 642 ], 643 "nodes": [ 644 { 645 "id": "transform1.output", 646 "type": "object", 647 "binding": { "nodeId": "transform1", "outputId": "output" } 648 } 649 ], 650 "variableUpdates": { 651 "transform1": [ 652 { 653 "variableId": "processedCount", 654 "expression": "=js:$vars.processedCount + $vars.transform1.output.count" 655 } 656 ] 657 } 658 }, 659 "nodes": [ 660 { 661 "id": "start", 662 "type": "core.trigger.manual", 663 "typeVersion": "1.0", 664 "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" }, 665 "inputs": { 666 "entryPointId": "" 667 }, 668 "outputs": { 669 "output": { 670 "type": "object", 671 "description": "Data passed when the flow is triggered manually.", 672 "source": "null", 673 "var": "output" 674 } 21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.

54	
55	```
56	<ProjectName>/
57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
60	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
61	├── operate.json            # runtime options
62	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest

65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
229	
230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.
